newsitem.title: USA: BPA peak firm power prices down $1 for Mon, Tues.
newsitem.headline: BPA peak firm power prices down $1 for Mon, Tues.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) cut prices for firm on-peak power for Monday and Tuesday by $1.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Friday.
BPA offered up to 300 megawatts of firm power during peak demand hours at $12.50 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $13.50 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Sunday firm peak power was offered at $9.50 for all deliveries.
Sunday through Tuesday firm off-peak prices were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
Non-firm power during peak hours (0800-1000, 1800-2000 PST) was offered at $16.00 (Northwest) and $17.00 (COB).
Non-firm prices for shoulder hours (0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200) were at $9.75 for Northwest and $10.75 for COB.
Non-firm power prices for off-peak (0100-0500 and 2400 PST) hours on Monday and Tuesday were raised by 25 cents to $9.25 for all deliveries.
BPA also offered displacement power during off-peak hours on Sunday at $6.00 and on Monday and Tuesday at $7.00 per MWh.
